name: Milcah (Daughter of Zelophehad)
title: Pioneer for Women's Inheritance Rights
summary: Milcah was one of five daughters of Zelophehad from the tribe of Manasseh. When their father died without sons, Milcah and her sisters approached Moses and demanded inheritance rights to their father's property. Their case led to a groundbreaking law that granted daughters the right to inherit when there were no sons.

keyEvents.title: Zelophehad's Daughters Present Their Case to Moses
keyEvents.description: Milcah and her four sisters stood before Moses, the priest Eleazar, the leaders, and the entire congregation at the entrance of the tent of meeting and demanded their father's inheritance share, since he had died without sons.

keyEvents.title: The Lord Grants Milcah and Her Sisters Their Request
keyEvents.description: God spoke to Moses and declared that the daughters of Zelophehad were right, commanding that their father's inheritance be given to them.

keyEvents.title: A new law of inheritance is established
keyEvents.description: The case of Milcah and her sisters led to a new law in Israel stating that inheritance should pass to daughters when there are no sons.

keyEvents.title: Marriage requirement for inheriting daughters
keyEvents.description: The leaders of the tribe of Manasseh were concerned that the inheritance would be lost from the tribe, so the Lord decreed that daughters who inherited land must marry within their own tribe.

keyEvents.title: Milcah and her sisters marry within their tribe
keyEvents.description: Milcah and her sisters obeyed the Lord's command and married men from the tribe of Manasseh, ensuring the inheritance remained within the tribe.

keyEvents.title: The inheritance is distributed in Canaan
keyEvents.description: When Joshua distributed the land, Milcah and her sisters came forward and received their inheritance among the tribe of Manasseh in the land of Canaan, as the Lord had commanded.
